title: Mag-Net Strong Anion Exchange for Ovarian Cancer Extracellular Vesicles Isolation
author: Tyler T. Cooper
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Murine ascites fluid (ID8 model of ovarian cancer, collected in-house)
Human ascites fluid (epithelial ovarian cancer, collected in-house) Reagents
MagReSyn TM SAX magnetic beads (ReSyn, catalog number: MR-SAX
LC–MS-grade 0.1% in water (Fisher Scientific, catalog number: LS
UPLC-grade 0.1% in acetonitrile (Fisher Scientific, catalog number: LS
BCA Peptide Quantification kit (Thermo Fisher, catalog number:

steps.title: Prepare all required buffers
steps.instruction: Make the following solutions using LC‑MS‑grade water: (1) Binding buffer (BB) pH 6.3: 50 mL total, add 1.412 g Bis‑Tris‑propane (100 mM), 439 mg NaCl (150 mM), then adjust to pH 6.3 with 5 N HCl (≈700–750 µL drop‑wise). Store at room temperature, use within 2 days. (2) Wash buffer (WB) pH 6.3: 50 mL total, add 0.706 g Bis‑Tris‑propane (50 mM), 439 mg NaCl (150 mM), adjust to pH 6.3 with 5 N HCl (≈200–300 µL). Store as above. (3) Elution buffer (EB) pH 6.3: 45 mL water + 5 mL 5 N HCl (≈200–300 µL) to reach 50 mL, add 0.706 g Bis‑Tris‑propane (50 mM), 2.92 g NaCl (1 M), 2.92 g Tween‑20 (1 % w/v). Store at room temperature, use within 2 days. (4) 1 % DDM stock: dissolve 100 mg n‑Dodecyl‑β‑D‑maltoside in 10 mL LC‑MS‑grade water (1 % w/v). Aliquot and store at –20 °C for up to 2 weeks. (5) Digestion buffer (DB) pH 8.0: 9.8 mL water, add 39.5 mg ammonium bicarbonate (50 mM) and 200 µL 1 % DDM stock (0.02 % w/v) to total 10 mL. Store at 4 °C, use within 2 days.

steps.title: Activate SAX magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend MagReSyn™ SAX bead slurry by gentle pipetting with a P200; invert to ensure homogeneity, reseal with parafilm and store at 4 °C. Transfer 100 µL slurry to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube, bring the tip to the tube bottom, place on a magnetic rack until clear (≈30–60 s), discard the storage buffer without disturbing the bead pellet. Add 500 µL pre‑equilibrated BB, resuspend gently (slow pipetting, low‑speed vortex, or gentle tapping). Re‑magnetize, discard supernatant. Repeat the BB wash (add 500 µL BB, resuspend, magnetize, discard) a total of six times. After the final wash, resuspend beads in 100 µL fresh BB, using the tip to the bottom to avoid bead loss on walls. Store activated beads at 4 °C (do not place on ice).

steps.title: Collect and clarify ascites fluid
steps.instruction: For murine ascites, aspirate 0.5–2.0 mL per mouse with a 1 mL syringe/26 G needle, transfer to a sterile 15 mL conical tube, keep on ice. For human ascites, collect 50–1 000 mL under anesthesia into a 500 mL sterile glass container, immediately transfer 50 mL to a sterile 50 mL conical tube on ice. Process all samples within 1–2 h. Aliquot 1.8 mL ascites into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube, centrifuge 1 000 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; transfer 1.6 mL supernatant to a new tube, avoiding the pellet. Optional: freeze‑aliquot clarified supernatant at –80 °C. Centrifuge the 1.6 mL at 10 000 × g, 10–20 min, 4 °C to remove debris and large vesicles; discard any floating fat/tissue layer. Transfer 80 % of the resulting supernatant to a fresh tube (cell‑free ascites). Aliquot the cell‑free ascites as desired (e.g., 100 µL per capture). Dilute each aliquot 1:1 with BB (e.g., 100 µL ascites + 100 µL BB) and mix gently.

steps.title: Capture EVs on SAX beads
steps.instruction: Equilibrate activated beads and diluted cell‑free ascites to room temperature. For each 200 µL diluted sample (100 µL ascites + 100 µL BB), add 25 µL activated SAX beads (bead:sample ratio 1:4). Gently mix by shaking or Thermomixer at 600 rpm for 2 min, then incubate at room temperature, 10–15 min with gentle agitation (600 rpm). Place tube on magnetic rack for 2 min, discard the unbound supernatant without disturbing the bead pellet (pipette from opposite side). Add 500 µL WB (adjust volume proportionally; recommend 5× input volume or 50 µL for <10 µL input). Resuspend gently for 2 min (600 rpm), re‑magnetize 2 min, discard wash supernatant. Repeat the WB wash (add 500 µL WB, resuspend 2 min, magnetize 2 min, discard) for a total of three washes. After the final wash, remove residual buffer carefully without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: On‑bead protein extraction and digestion
steps.instruction: Resuspend the bead‑EV pellet in 50–55 µL lysis buffer (4 M urea, 50 mM Tris pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 2 % SDS, 1 % NP‑40). Mix gently (pipette or low‑speed vortex). Incubate 24 °C, 15 min with gentle shaking (600–800 rpm). (Optional) Remove 5 µL for BCA protein quantification. Add TCEP to a final concentration of 5–10 mM, then add IAA to 30 mM; incubate in the dark at 24 °C, 800 rpm for 30 min (cover tube with foil). Add acetonitrile to reach 70 % (e.g., add 117 µL ACN to 50 µL lysate). Incubate 24 °C, 800 rpm, 15 min. Magnetize 2 min, discard supernatant. Add 200 µL 80 % ethanol while beads remain on the magnet, incubate 2 min, then aspirate supernatant. Repeat ethanol wash two more times (total three ethanol washes). Add 200 µL 95 % acetonitrile, incubate 2 min, discard supernatant, then remove tube from magnet. Add 100 µL DB directly to the bead pellet; pipette to disperse beads (brief water‑bath sonication <3 s if needed). Add Lys‑C at 1:100 (w/w) enzyme‑to‑protein ratio, incubate 37 °C, 2 h, 900 rpm. Add trypsin (or other protease) at 1:25–1:50 (w/w) ratio, incubate 37 °C, 12–16 h (or 2 h for rapid protocol) on Thermomixer at 900 rpm.

steps.title: Peptide cleanup and LC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Terminate digestion by acidifying to pH < 3 with 10 % TFA (final 1–2 %). Optional: wash once with LC‑MS‑grade water or DB to recover residual peptides. Centrifuge 16 000 × g, 10 min, RT; transfer supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube. Desalt peptides using C18 StageTips or SPE cartridges per manufacturer’s instructions (skip desalting for samples derived from <10 µL starting ascites). Elute peptides with 60 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid. Dry eluates in a vacuum concentrator to ≤10 µL. Reconstitute in 0.1 % formic acid containing 0.01 % DDM (10–100 µL) for LC‑MS/MS. Load 50–500 ng peptide onto the LC‑MS/MS system, run in data‑independent acquisition with gas‑phase fractionation (GPF‑DIA). For low‑input samples (<10 µL ascites), consider FAIMS or other ion‑mobility enhancements.

steps.title: Optional EV elution for downstream assays
steps.instruction: After the final wash in step C, resuspend the bead‑EV pellet in 100–200 µL EB. Mix gently by slow pipetting (avoid vigorous pipetting). Incubate RT, 10–15 min with gentle agitation on Thermomixer at 400 rpm. Place on magnetic rack, allow beads to separate, then transfer the EV‑containing supernatant to a low‑protein‑binding tube. (Optional) Repeat elution with fresh EB and pool eluates (note that repeated elution dilutes EV concentration). Adjust buffer for downstream use: dilute in particle‑free PBS for NTA, add SDS sample buffer for western blot, or follow EM preparation protocols. Use 10 kDa or 100 kDa ultrafiltration devices for buffer exchange if needed. Store eluted EVs on ice (short‑term) or at –80 °C (long‑term); minimize freeze‑thaw cycles.
